$comment: The browser-check suite manifest: one entry per scripts/**/*-playwright-checks.js.
scripts/run-playwright-suite.js reads this instead of the bash for-loop that used
to live in docs/ui-tests/deb-install-validation.md section 6, where the tier, the
per-check timeout and the run-last rule were two case statements and a comment.
scripts/playwright-suite-manifest.test.js fails the build when a check exists with
no entry here, or an entry names a script that does not exist, so the manifest
cannot drift away from the suite.
name        the --only/--skip handle; the script basename without the suffix.
script      repo-relative path, so the runner never guesses at a filename.
tiers       smoke      the CI tier: fast, no fixtures beyond the demo dataset.
core       needs a running deployment and the demo database.
extended   needs a fixture or a runtime the standard pass lacks.
live-external needs a live third-party account and spends real transmissions
(the scripts/e2e/fax SRFax loopback set). Only ever a manual entry:
it runs when named with --only, never from any tier.
standalone needs no Tomcat, no database and no login at all.
front-door only meaningful through the packaged nginx + ModSecurity
front door, where a WAF exists to false-positive on
clinical prose; through bare Tomcat that half proves
nothing. A check can be in this tier and one other.
assertsDatabase  the check reads the rows that reached MariaDB, so it needs
MYSQL_* and must not be pointed at a shared database.
provinces   all, or the billregion values the check is written for.
timeoutSec  wall clock the runner allows before it gives up on the check.
runLast     the check is destructive to shared state (deliberate failed logins)
and must run after the positive suite.
manual      the check is never part of a tier run: it needs explicit
fixture permissions or credentials beyond the common contract
(for example, the installer's initial-admin.txt). It runs only
when named with --only.
env         environment variables beyond the common contract in
lib/playwright-harness.js readConfig(). Extracted from each script;
defaults and meanings belong in the scripts own header comment.
expectedFailure  { finding, step }. The check asserts correct behaviour and fails
at that step while a logged defect stands. finding is a row of
docs/ui-tests/app-findings-log.md whose status is not fixed; step is the
label the script gives s.step(). The runner reports known-fail (failed
there; does not fail the run), unexpected-pass (passed; reported) and
failed-elsewhere (any other failure, cleanup included; fails the run).
A script that labels no steps cannot carry one. notes may add the detail.
mutates     the clinic-wide objects the check changes: a table name, property:<name>
(or UserProperty:<name>) for property rows, or file:<label> for something
on disk. The runner's --residue-audit snapshots fax_config, encounterForm and
the named property rows before the first check and reports any difference
after the last; other entries are listed in its output as not diffed.
A check that mutates more than the audit log must say in fixtures that it
must not run concurrently with other checks (live wrapper: EXCLUSIVE=1).
TIERS ARE A FIRST CUT. They were assigned from each checks dependencies, not
from a measured run; the smoke list is the one in the coverage plan. Adjust them
in the PR that measures the tier, not by guess.

checks.name: allergy-add-penicillin
checks.notes: Adds a Penicillins allergy through the allergy page's Penicillin shortcut, checks the chart and amends it (archive plus replacement). The shortcut records an ATC class allergen (#4576): the reaction form carries TYPECODE 8, the class code J01C and no DrugRef id, and both rows are stored that way. Last, for app-findings-log.md finding 178 (fixed): both the added allergy and its amendment carry the ATC class code J01C and no regional_identifier (a class has no DIN), and RxAddAllergy2Action logs no ERROR in the run's window of the server journal (CARLOS_LOG_JOURNAL_UNIT; without it the check ends SKIP after its row assertions). Until #4576 the shortcut posted DrugRef id 44452, which the packaged DrugRef holds as a multivitamin brand, so both identifiers were empty. The script is a runCheck script whose stages before step 6 are unlabelled; the stored rows and the run's window of the server journal are READ in a labelled step of their own ("the added allergy and its amendment are stored, and this run's window of the server journal is read"), so a journal it cannot read is a failure elsewhere.

checks.name: allergy-class-shortcut-alert
checks.notes: Issue #4576, finding 215: the Penicillin and Sulfa shortcuts record the ATC class allergens J01C and J01E (TYPECODE 8, no DrugRef id), and the drug-allergy check decides them by their class code, while DrugRef is also asked about the class under its AHFS and its ATC name. Prescribing Amoxil (J01CA04) warns on the shortcut's penicillin allergy and on one the old shortcut recorded (drugref_id 44452, TYPECODE 10, seeded by SQL) and on no sulfonamide allergy; Septra (J01EE01) warns on both sulfonamide allergies only. Products the DPD files outside the ATC class still warn through the AHFS class: HP-PAC (A02BD07) on both penicillin allergies, BLEPHAMIDE (S01CA02) on both sulfonamide allergies. Biaxin (J01FA09) warns on none and leaves none "not checked". Each prescribing step first asserts the picked drug's ATC code, so a DrugRef extract without the product fails as such. Amending the old Sulfa shortcut's allergy stores the replacement as ATC class J01E. Each prescribing step runs in a fresh login, because the Rx stash is per session; with rx_show_highest_allergy_warning on, a step expects only the most severe match. The drug search terms are ALLERGY_CLASS_PENICILLIN_DRUG, ALLERGY_CLASS_SULFONAMIDE_DRUG, ALLERGY_CLASS_PENICILLIN_COMBINATION_DRUG, ALLERGY_CLASS_SULFONAMIDE_COMBINATION_DRUG and ALLERGY_CLASS_OTHER_DRUG (defaults amoxil, septra, hp-pac, blephamide, biaxin). Needs DrugRef with AHFS (the packaged extract carries it).
checks.fixtures: Owned FAKE- patient (runWorkflow): the two allergies the shortcuts record, two seeded with the old shortcuts' identity, and the amendment; cleanup deletes every allergies row of that patient and asserts none remain, then the patient. checks.name: consultation-fax-account
checks.notes: Issue #5278. Letterhead ▸ Fax Account with two owned active senders and one inactive: the selector offers the active ones by number and name; Submit And Fax with the non-default sender opens the cover page on that sender (release/2026.08 compared the posted number with the account id and fell back to another sender, finding 327) and saves one referral; Send queues one job from exactly that sender's line and user, to the consultant, for the owned patient, logged against the referral, with a PDF of this referral in the document store; Update And Fax with the other sender does the same without a second referral; Cancel queues nothing; a sender deactivated after it was chosen is not replaced (no account selected) and Send is refused with an alert; two windows at once (E-Chart and clinic list) keep their own senders and patients. The senders are MIDDLEWARE accounts on an unroutable loopback relay with no inbound polling, so nothing leaves the host (a running scheduler fails the job at the provider boundary); consultation-fax-account-transport drives the relay call. Skips without consultation fax or the _fax right, and where any other fax sender account is active. Needs pdftotext and read access to the document store (CONSULT_FAX_DOCUMENT_STORE, default the packaged path).

checks.name: consultation-fax-account-transport
checks.notes: Issue #5278, transport. A local relay stub on 127.0.0.1 (FAX_TRANSPORT_STUB_PORT, default 18096) stands in for the fax provider: after Update And Fax ▸ Send from sender A, the fax scheduler (started from Configure Fax when stopped) calls the stub once, as A only (A's site credentials, fax user and fax password, the consultant as destination, A's fax line) with a document byte-identical to the PDF the job names, and the job is SENT with the stub's job id; a send from B, which the stub refuses with HTTP 500, leaves B's job in ERROR (Problem communicating with fax service) and is never retried through A. Manual: needs the operator prerequisite below; SKIPs without FAX_TRANSPORT_STUB=on. Needs pdftotext.
checks.fixtures: Operator prerequisite: add -Dcarlos.fax.middleware.allowedHosts=127.0.0.1 to CARLOS_JAVA_OPTS in /etc/carlos-emr/carlos-emr.env, carlos-ctl restart, export FAX_TRANSPORT_STUB=on; afterwards remove the option and restart again. Owned FAKE patient, service, consultant (lib/consultation-referral-fixture.js) and service link seeded by SQL; the service and consultant are in the clinic-wide pickers while the run lasts, so the check must not run concurrently with other checks (live wrapper: EXCLUSIVE=1). Two owned MIDDLEWARE fax_config rows pointed at the stub (download off), clinic-wide while the run lasts. If the fax scheduler was stopped the check starts it, as an administrator would; once the accounts are removed its cycles have nothing to send. The demo database carries EFormDocs rows (attached documents, labs, forms, HRM reports and eForms) for ids 247-1063 that no eform_data row owns, so a new instance whose id falls there inherits them and a login without read access to those object types is refused 403 before the eForm is stored ("no permission to use one or more selected attachments"); the workflow therefore moves the id counter past them first, or the control step would fail depending on the id it happened to get. The POST-replay step failed once in an earlier run of this plan with its message lost and did not fail in 22 later runs (16 through the runner, 6 replay-only under four busy CPU cores): see the Task 15 report. Its failure messages now carry the AddEForm statuses and the owned-row count. The finding-168 step needs the eForm PDF renderer: before passing it, the check downloads one of the run's saved eForms (eform/downloadEFormPdf); when no PDF comes back, Add to Documents never reached the document step, and the check SKIPs there rather than passing the pinned step.

checks.name: authz-read-chart-note-history
checks.fixtures: Seven owned patients with notes, numeric measurements and CPP issue links; shared authz fixture with module readers and er_clerk/doctor logins. Two owned programs use preexisting cached reporter roles and an unchanged global policy, with one existing Facility bound through the owned reader only. All clinical descendants, program memberships/admissions, audit rows, roles and logins are removed and verified; shared defaults and policies remain unchanged. Requires pdftotext; availability is checked before fixture creation. Additional isolated startup and group-note fixtures own their patients, providers, facilities, programs, admissions, links, notes and policies; preexisting clinical rows and policies are compared exactly, and every owned row is removed. Additional compact-save, issue-history and form fixtures own their patients, programs, notes, issue links and separate module-granted logins; native form creation uses the existing guarded VT catalog lifecycle. Vascular Tracker first-use catalog rows are recorded before any native form opens and only proven fixture-created definitions are removed after clinical children; preexisting definitions, IDs and validation rows remain exact. This check must not run concurrently with other checks (live wrapper: EXCLUSIVE=1).
checks.notes: Both history routes enforce patient identity, record locks and notes-module access. Independent module-granted readers exercise six measurement/navbar GET routes, both measurement writer aliases and three web print routes plus REST print with record-only denials and unlocked controls. Complete clinical/draft/lock snapshots survive refusals; allowed writers persist one exact reading, HTML retains UTF-8/literal markup and PDFs contain the owned note. Malformed print identities and foreign/mixed HTML selection refuse without partial output. Native chart controls establish a real reporter-role denial and readable cross-program notes before testing actual selected/ALL/date/CPP/Other Meds/full PDFs. REST signed-context checks preserve that visibility despite another program entered last, both wrong patient query aliases or program-zero hints, reject hidden selections and forged/conflicting genuine contexts, and retain an independently authorized other-program positive. Fresh configured-provider program-zero entries are refused through both aliases, while sole-program defaults and genuinely programless zero entries render their own native chart and editor. Active group-note recipients can expand the native long-note view under the existing group reporter policy; editor/raw access, inactive links or unlinked notes, missing record access, disabled facilities and wrong reporter roles are refused without changing source notes. Two same-patient editors retain independent note locks through a native compact save and the other editor's full Save; an exact foreign-session lock refusal preserves all clinical and draft state. Captured-program issue history retains readable cross-program notes and refuses hidden reporter notes and record exclusions. Genuine form-only readers without chart or program access can create and reopen their own form; record-only exclusions refuse both setup and save, and GET, HEAD and PUT mutations return 405 before data changes.

checks.name: direct-response-contract
checks.notes: The direct responses outside the Struts route measurement: /servlet/BackupDownload, /servlet/OscarDownload, admin/ViewAdminBackupDownload and admin/ViewOscarLogging. The administrator is served the EXACT bytes of a seeded marker file (not valid UTF-8) with Content-Disposition attachment, nosniff and a matching Content-Length by BackupDownload (armed through billing/CA/ON/moveMOHFiles, the one readable directory a BackupDownload session can have on the packaged install), by OscarDownload's obecdownload key (DOCUMENT_DIR, armed by oscarReport/obec; the marker is named in the shape the application writes, OBECE + 13 digits + .TXT) and ohipdownload key (HOME_DIR, armed by ViewBillingONMRI; marker H + month letter + 6 digits + .999). Doctor, nurse and receptionist (authz-read-fixture logins) are refused by every route with the application's own 403 (h.assertRefused: its header or error page, never the front door's page) and nothing is served; OscarDownload checks no privilege and serves only a session that opened its page, so it refuses a cold session, serves a role that opened a page its role may open (doctor: OBEC and OHIP; receptionist: OHIP) and refuses the roles whose page refuses them. A session without a login gets the application's 401 from the servlets and a redirect to /logoutPage from the pages. The log viewer's gate is the intended OR (ViewOscarLogging2Action admits _admin or _admin.reporting): a login holding only _admin.reporting r is served the viewer (200, #logForm) and refused by BackupDownload and the backup page, and a login holding neither object is refused; the gate action ignores SERVERLOGGING (only the Administration menu entry, admin.jsp:505, checks it). Traversal: the front door blocks the literal ../x forms before the application sees them (28 of 80 probes per run: reported as application not reached, never counted as the application's refusal; no direct Tomcat port exists to repeat them), so the check also sends the shapes the front door lets through (a nested marker file reached by /, %2f and %5c, a drive or absolute prefix, hidden and script file names, unknown homepath keys, a missing filename or key) and requires the application's 400 (not another refusal) for each, with a nested marker file in place to prove nothing below the served directory is read. Every attachment is the file and never an HTML page, and no error is sent as an attachment. The application reads its properties at start, so the check does not change them and does not restart: it seeds into the directories the installed configuration uses and records a SKIP line (the step still passes) for a row whose directory the service cannot use. On the packaged install two rows are skipped: admin/ViewAdminBackupDownload (backup_path=/home/mysql/ does not exist on the host and ProtectHome=yes hides /home from the service; the page says Backup directory not found) and the log viewer's content (LOGGING_PATH is not set; the page says Logging path is not configured). Their seeded-file branches (listing and exact bytes from backup_path, the log rendered HTML-encoded, an invalid report type) have not run against a live install. Ontario only for the OHIP and MOH rows (they skip when billregion is not ON); BC has not been run (issue #4439). Expected to FAIL at the last step 'OscarDownload (OBEC key) refuses a stored-document file to a login that holds no _edoc': a login holding only _report r (a role the check creates; it can open oscarReport/obec and nothing else, and cannot grant itself rights) opens the OBEC page and is served a stored-document marker from DOCUMENT_DIR (finding 202); every earlier step passes. The two least-privilege logins are created only after the steps that use the doctor on a multi-object page, because their role rows change the order in which the database returns the privilege rows and the doctor then loses the OBEC page (finding 205; not pinned by a check of its own). If finding 202 is fixed by limiting the key to the files the application generates, the controls stay valid; a fix of another kind (a per-file token, a privilege check) changes them. Not covered, logged as finding 203: a missing file answers HTTP 500 with an uncaught exception, which the check does not repeat so a run adds no ERROR stack to the journal.

expectedFailure.step: OscarDownload (OBEC key) refuses a stored-document file to a login that holds no _edoc

Steps: the Ontario install, the paths (ONEDT_OUTBOX and the billing region from the environment or CARLOS_PROPERTIES_FILE; any other billregion SKIPs with the reason); the mailbox opens through the Administration shell with its four tabs and the Upload tab's Add, Delete Selected and Submit (Submit is inspected, never clicked); an OHIP diskette is generated for an owned provider the way billing-on-group-disk-zero-total does; Add writes the fixture claim file to the outbox byte for byte (bytes that are not UTF-8) and lists it once; Add refuses a non-claim name, a month letter beyond L, ../, a leading /, a sub-directory and a hidden name with the application's message and writes nothing (..\ and C: are blocked by the front door and counted as application not reached); Delete Selected removes only the ticked file (an OBEC-shaped bystander and a file beside the outbox survive) and refuses a list with a path in it; Change Password creates the property and the second change replaces it in the same row, and neither the page nor any response echoes the typed text (the stored value is not judged here: finding 189 pins it); controls with a valid token for Delete, Add and Change Password, then GET and a tokenless POST of each pass h.assertRefused (the application's own 403/405, never the front door's page) and change neither the outbox, the directory beside it nor the property; a doctor (holds _billing, not _admin.billing) is refused on all four routes and all three mutators, and a login holding _admin.billing r only is served the pages and refused all three mutators with a valid token. checks.notes: The multi-facility login, driven through the login form as a throwaway provider who belongs to two enabled facilities (coverage plan: login-facility-chooser). Steps: the login is sent to /select_facility straight after its password and the chooser lists exactly its two facilities (by id and name; a third facility it is not in is absent); a typed Schedule URL and a typed chart URL are each redirected to the chooser by the application (HTTP 302) and a browser that follows lands on the chooser, not on the Schedule, the chart, an error page or a blank page; the chooser stage audits no facility; Logout (/logoutPage, as the Schedule's logout button does; the chooser has no logout control of its own) ends the session, writes one log out row, and the Schedule URL then goes to the logout page and not the chooser; a second sign-in that presses facility A's button reaches the Schedule and writes exactly one log in row with contentId facilityId=<A> and the client address; controls prove the same typed Schedule and chart URLs are served after the pick (so the redirects were the pending choice) and that the stylesheet and script the chooser links are real files; A's banner shows A's live message and not B's, not C's (a facility the login is not in) and not A's expired one; a third sign-in picking B shows B's message only and audits facilityId=<B> once; a one-facility login (facility B) reaches the Schedule without requesting /select_facility, audits facilityId=<B> once, is served the chart and sees only B's banner message; every owned row is removed and asserted gone, and Administration > Facilities (the reader of the facility cache) then lists none of the run's facilities. LAST AND PINNED to finding 265: the chooser page's own stylesheet (/css/caisi_css.css) and script (/js/global.js), linked by caisi_html_top.jspf, are answered HTTP 302 to /select_facility while the choice is pending (LoginFilter.PENDING_FACILITY_SELECTION_URLS lists neither), so the browser refuses the chooser's HTML as a stylesheet and a script and the page renders unstyled with two console errors on every multi-facility sign-in. Every step before the pin passes today; the other steps assert the page's browser signals (console, failed requests, bad responses) of the throwaway logins' pages except those two blocked files, which only the pinned step judges. Expected: the pin fails and everything else passes.
checks.fixtures: Two throwaway logins with the seeded doctor role in the test login's programs (own provider rows 800000-899999, a copy of the test login's credential; authzReadFixture), three Facility rows named after the run marker (A and B enabled and joined by the logins, C joined by nobody; cloned from an existing facility's configuration columns), provider_facility rows (two-facility login: A and B; one-facility login: B), four facility_message rows (A live, A expired, B live, C live) and the run's owned FAKE patient for the chart URL. The Facility rows are visible in Administration > Facilities while the run lasts; no existing facility, property, flag or clinic-wide row is read for update or changed. Cleanup removes the messages, facilities, logins, their provider_facility, preference and audit rows by key and asserts each gone; the facility cache is not populated by login, so nothing stale remains.

checks.name: admin-lot-number-delete
checks.notes: Administration > Search lot number by prevention > a lot > Delete (admin/ViewLotNrDeleteRecordHtm, then a POST to admin/LotNrDeleteRecord). Two lots of an owned prevention type are seeded, one carrying an apostrophe, double quotes and an ampersand. The search for that type lists exactly both, each linking to its own delete page; the target's link opens the delete page filled in with exactly its type and lot; Delete posts exactly those, the result page says the record was deleted, the target row is soft-deleted (deleted=1, nothing else changed but the update time the entity stamps) and the control row is unchanged; a new search lists the control only; with the lot number cleared, Delete raises the page's "must be entered" alert and posts nothing; a GET and HEAD replay of the real delete POST aimed at the control lot passes h.assertRefused and leaves it undeleted. No known defect. The replay is sent from the page (a same-origin fetch) rather than the context's request client, because the session cookie is Secure and only the browser sends it over plain HTTP to a loopback origin (issue #4718); the check therefore runs on an HTTP or HTTPS base URL alike. Passes on develop (231f36a0e2, Ontario): 2 of 2 runs over HTTP and 1 over HTTPS. Run on Ontario only; not yet run on BC (issue #4439), so provinces is the planned value until Task 27 corrects it from a real BC run.

checks.name: chart-context-request-guards
checks.fixtures: Three owned synthetic patients, saved notes and an issue link, chart drafts and lock rows; owned roles/logins for registry and issue-write refusals; transient triggers scoped to the exact owned draft and issue deletion force real rollback and are removed and verified. The issue trigger fires after its exact row is deleted and only when the new owned note revision exists inside the transaction. Requires CREATE/DROP TRIGGER in the disposable database; must not run concurrently with other checks (live wrapper: EXCLUSIVE=1).
checks.notes: Signed context forgery, cross-patient and cross-login replay, conflicting parameters, foreign note edit/history/draft references and GET autosave refusal preserve complete clinical rows; registry module and record locks refuse with 403. Issue-only write access cannot partially delete an issue attached to a saved note. A database failure after issue deletion preserves every clinical row, the persisted draft and exact editor lock; the same editor retries successfully and removes only its superseded draft. Actual autosave database failure preserves the prior draft, reports failure visibly and recovers on retry, including network failures, cleared text and the legacy editor. A real 45-second native XHR timeout releases the save guard and allows retry. HTTP 200 login HTML cannot acknowledge a saved draft in either editor; the implicit existing-note legacy editor submits its actual selected ID. A real lost-lock autosave causes HTTP 409: Cancel retains raw editor text and the last acknowledged draft; native reload acquires a fresh owned lock, and retry autosaves the retained raw text. Passive browser protocol observations associate at most one canceled old-document release beacon with its exact request and later application response, preserving every unrelated diagnostic.
